verdict: Veeva grew revenue 18% to $928M as Vault CRM had its best quarter ever, and GAAP profit jumped 37% to $273M.

segments.name: Subscription services
segments.note: Cloud software subscriptions for life-sciences companies — up 16% YoY. Within it, R&D and Quality Solutions brought in $419M and Commercial Solutions $347M.

segments.name: Professional services
segments.note: Consulting, implementation and other services — up 24% YoY.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the Vault platform and new AI agents — up 16% YoY.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Selling subscriptions and services — up 16% YoY.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day — down from $96M a year ago, when it included a $31M litigation settlement charge.

otherDetail: Other income, net — mostly interest on Veeva's cash and short-term investments. The release reports $75M ($74.5M); shown as $74M so the figures, rounded to whole $M, balance exactly.
footerNote: Veeva's fiscal Q3 (ended October 31, 2026) had not been reported as of November 7, 2026 — this is the latest reported quarter.

takeaways.title: Growth picked up
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 18% to $928M — subscription revenue up 16% to $767M and professional services up 24% to $161M. Veeva also raised its full-year outlook.

takeaways.title: Profit jumped 37%
takeaways.text: GAAP net income was $273M, up 37% from $200M a year ago, helped by last year's quarter carrying a $31M litigation charge in G&A. Non-GAAP net income was $387M.

takeaways.title: Vault CRM is winning
takeaways.text: More than 180 customers are live on Vault CRM, including five top-20 biopharmas, in what Veeva called its best CRM quarter ever — and its new AI agents are the next pitch.
